_about: What good looks like, per weakness class (agent/grouping.py weakness_class, plus the secret and dependency categories). Written by GapScan from the bundled OWASP Cheat Sheet Series snapshot (data/owasp/cheatsheets); each entry names its sheet. Shown to the deep-dive model as trusted guidance. 'signals' are code-shaped texts whose presence would show the control exists; the model searches them before claiming a control is missing.

controls.control: Prepared statements / parameterized queries: the query text is constant and values are bound separately
Allow-list validation for parts that cannot be parameters (table or column names, sort order)

sql-injection.fix: Use a parameterized query with the driver's placeholder (for example sqlite3: execute("... WHERE name = ?", (name,)); SQLAlchemy: text() with bound parameters). Keep allow-list validation only for identifiers that cannot be parameters.
not_a_fix: Escaping or stripping quotes by hand instead of binding parameters
Only validating input while still concatenating it into SQL
verify: No query in the project is built by string concatenation or formatting with request data
A value containing a quote is treated as data (returns no rows, raises no SQL error)

controls.control: Avoid calling OS commands: use a library/API for the task
If a command is unavoidable: no shell, arguments as a list
Allow-list validation of every user-supplied argument

command-injection.fix: Prefer a library call over a command. If a command is unavoidable, call it without a shell with the arguments as a list, and validate each user-supplied argument against an allow-list (for a host: parse it as an IP address or hostname first).
not_a_fix: Blocking a few characters such as ; or & (deny-lists are bypassed)
Quoting the whole command string while still using shell=True
verify: No call passes request data to a shell
An argument containing shell metacharacters is rejected or passed literally

controls.control: Untrusted data is parsed with a data-only format
If native serialization must be used: integrity check (signature) before deserializing

deserialization.fix: Do not deserialize untrusted data with pickle (or yaml.load / jsonpickle); accept a data-only format such as JSON and validate it against the expected schema. If native objects must cross a trust boundary, sign them and verify the signature before loading.
not_a_fix: Checking the size or type of the payload before pickle.loads
verify: No pickle/yaml.load call reads request data
The endpoint rejects a payload that is not valid JSON

controls.control: Passwords: a slow, salted password hash
Integrity or signatures (not passwords): SHA-256 or stronger

weak-hash.fix: Decide by purpose. For passwords use Argon2id (at least 19 MiB memory, 2 iterations, parallelism 1); if unavailable scrypt; bcrypt (work factor 10 or more) for legacy; PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with 600,000+ iterations where FIPS-140 is required. Rehash existing passwords at next login. For integrity checks use SHA-256 or stronger. A non-security use (cache key, ETag) is not a vulnerability.
not_a_fix: Replacing MD5 with SHA-256 (or any fast hash) for passwords: fast hashes are not password hashes
verify: Stored password hashes use the chosen password-hashing algorithm and parameters
Old MD5 hashes are migrated on next login and then removed

controls.control: Context-aware output encoding, ideally by a template engine that escapes by default
HTML sanitization when HTML input must be allowed

xss.fix: Return data through a template engine with autoescaping (or encode it for the exact output context), and set an explicit non-HTML content type for data responses. Sanitize with a vetted library only where HTML must be allowed.
not_a_fix: Encoding for the wrong context (HTML encoding inside a JavaScript string)
verify: A value containing <script> is shown as text, not executed
Data responses carry a non-HTML content type

controls.control: The image switches to an unprivileged user (rule #2)
No privilege escalation in the container (rule #4)

container-root.fix: Create an unprivileged user in the Dockerfile (for example RUN groupadd -r app && useradd -r -g app app) and switch to it with USER before the entrypoint; run with --security-opt=no-new-privileges.
not_a_fix: Only documenting that the container should be run with -u
verify: docker inspect shows a non-root Config.User
The process inside the running container is not uid 0

controls.control: Canonicalize the path and check it stays inside the allowed base directory
Allow-list or generated file names

path-traversal.fix: Resolve the requested path to its canonical form and reject it unless it is inside the base directory; better, map user input to an allow-listed or generated file name.
verify: A request for ../ or an absolute path is rejected

controls.control: Allow-list of destination hosts or URLs
Block private, loopback and link-local addresses after resolution

ssrf.fix: Only allow requests to an allow-list of destinations; when that is impossible, resolve the host and block private, loopback and link-local addresses, and disable redirects.
not_a_fix: Checking the URL string for 'localhost' or '127.0.0.1'
verify: A request to an internal address is refused

controls.control: Server-side secrets come from the environment or a secrets manager, not source code
On mobile, keys are generated and kept in the platform keystore (Android Keystore, iOS Keychain), never shipped in the app

secret.fix: Treat the credential as exposed in every build that contains it: a constant compiled into an app can be extracted from that build even where the code path that uses it never runs. Revoke and rotate it first; then, server side, load it from the environment or a secrets manager, and in a mobile app generate the key in the platform keystore on the device (or fetch a short-lived credential from a backend), migrating data protected by the old secret. Remove it from source and purge it from git history, and add a secret scanner to CI.
not_a_fix: Deleting the line without rotating the credential: it stays valid and stays in git history
Keeping a hardcoded fallback secret for some builds or flavors: it still ships in every build that compiles it
verify: A secret scan of the full git history finds nothing

controls.control: The dependency is pinned at or above the fixed version

dependency.fix: Upgrade to the fixed version and re-run the tests. If no fixed version exists, apply the advisory's mitigation (or a virtual patch) and document the accepted risk until one does.
verify: The manifest and lockfile declare the fixed version
A rescan no longer reports the advisory
